config.description: v023's exact recipe and architecture with ONE change: distill_weight 0.5 -> 1.0. Same hidden 128 (225,922 params), same teacher (dozken's reset2k replayed as exact labels), same loss otherwise, same optimiser, same batch 16, 3 epochs, chunk 1,000, state reset every 2,000. This is the distillation-weight experiment and nothing else.
config.hypothesis: Our students land BELOW their teacher, which is the signature of too LITTLE teacher signal rather than too much. The evidence is quantitative and matched on compression: dozken's distil160 is 72% of his teacher and GAINED +0.0009 over it, while our v022 at 74% LOST -0.0049 against the same teacher. That is a ~0.006 shortfall in our distillation at equal compression. Meanwhile the student sits between the two things it is trained on: hard-labels-only (v021) scores 0.678575, the teacher scores 0.690168, and v023 scores 0.684681 -- roughly midway, so doubling the teacher term should pull it toward the teacher without anything else changing. If it does, the knob is real and 2.0 is the next value; if it does not, the shortfall is not the WEIGHT of the teacher signal but its CONTENT, which points at feature distillation instead.
config.change_vs_parent: distill_weight 0.5 -> 1.0 ONLY. The term is dw * weighted_MSE(teacher_clipped, pred_clipped), so this doubles the teacher term against an unchanged weighted-Pearson hard-label term -- the teacher goes from ~1/3 to ~1/2 of the total gradient.
